<!-- Generated by scripts/build_practice.py from practice/source. Edit the source, then rebuild. -->

Set a timer for **130 minutes** for 65 questions, the same two minutes per question as the real exam. Choose one answer unless the question says otherwise. 7 questions ask for more than one answer. Write down your answer and flag every guess before you open the answers.

## Question 1

A partner uploads daily instrument exports to an on-premises NFS share. The lab wants the files copied to S3 every night, with only changed files transferred and integrity verified, without writing scripts. Which service should it use?

- **A.** AWS Transfer Family with an SFTP endpoint that the partner's share pushes files to
- **B.** AWS DataSync with an agent on premises and a scheduled task to the S3 bucket
- **C.** AWS DMS with a full load task that treats the NFS share as a source endpoint
- **D.** Amazon AppFlow with a scheduled flow from the file share to the S3 bucket

## Question 2

An instrument control API must read the current configuration for a device in microseconds at very high request rates. The data must survive node failures without a separate database behind it. Which store fits best?

- **A.** Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey in front of an Aurora PostgreSQL cluster
- **B.** Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity and strongly consistent reads
- **C.** Amazon MemoryDB as the primary database for device configuration
- **D.** Amazon Redshift with the configuration table using DISTSTYLE ALL

## Question 3

A Python script must list all objects under a prefix that holds 30,000 files and start a Glue job for each date found. A first version only processed 1,000 files. What should the engineer change?

- **A.** Use the Boto3 paginator for list_objects_v2 to read every page of results
- **B.** Raise the MaxKeys parameter on list_objects_v2 to 30,000 in a single request
- **C.** Switch to the S3 Select API so the script reads the bucket listing as one CSV
- **D.** Call the Glue StartCrawler API instead and read the file list from CloudTrail

## Question 4

A company adds new research projects every week. Each project's S3 objects are tagged with project=<name>, and each researcher's IAM role is tagged with the projects they belong to. Security wants one policy that keeps working as projects are added. Which approach fits?

- **A.** Create a new IAM policy for every project and attach it to the members' roles
- **B.** Create one IAM group per project and add each researcher's IAM user to it
- **C.** Use a bucket policy that lists every researcher's role ARN under each prefix
- **D.** Use an ABAC condition matching the object's project tag to the role's tag

## Question 5

A nightly Redshift load must include exactly the 48 files that an upstream job produced for the day. Last week a late file was silently skipped because COPY loaded whatever was under the prefix at the time. What should the engineer change?

- **A.** Add a sleep step of 30 minutes before the COPY so late files have time to arrive
- **B.** Split each file into smaller parts so the COPY finishes before late files arrive
- **C.** Have the upstream job write a manifest of all 48 files, then COPY with MANIFEST
- **D.** Run a crawler on the prefix before the COPY to register the files in the catalog

## Question 6

Analysts across the company cannot find trusted datasets and keep asking the data team what columns mean and who owns them. Leadership wants a searchable catalog with business definitions, owners, and a request-and-approve process for access. What should the data team use?

- **A.** Amazon SageMaker Catalog with glossary terms, metadata forms, and subscription requests
- **B.** The AWS Glue Data Catalog with table descriptions filled in by a weekly crawler
- **C.** A Confluence page per dataset with a form that emails the data team for access
- **D.** Lake Formation LF-Tags on each table plus an SNS topic for access requests

## Question 7

An audit finds that 400 CloudWatch log groups created by Lambda and Glue keep data forever, and log storage cost is rising. Security requires one year of retention for every existing group and for every group created in future. **Choose TWO.**

- **A.** Set a 365-day retention period on every existing log group
- **B.** Change the log class of each existing group to Essentials
- **C.** Export all groups to S3 nightly and delete the original groups
- **D.** Create log groups with 365-day retention in the IaC templates
- **E.** Add a metric filter on each group that alarms on stored bytes

## Question 8

A Glue job connects to Aurora PostgreSQL using a username and password stored in the job's script. Security requires the password to rotate every 30 days automatically, with no code changes after each rotation. What should the team do?

- **A.** Store the password as a Parameter Store SecureString and update it with a scheduled script
- **B.** Store the password in an encrypted environment variable on the Glue job definition
- **C.** Store it in Secrets Manager with managed rotation and read the secret from the job
- **D.** Create a new IAM user for the job every 30 days and delete the previous user

## Question 9

A Glue job must run at 06:15 every weekday in the lab's local time zone, and the schedule must adjust automatically for daylight saving time. Which option meets this with the least effort?

- **A.** A Glue trigger with a cron expression written in UTC for the winter offset
- **B.** A Lambda function that sleeps until 06:15 local time and then starts the job
- **C.** An EventBridge rule with a rate expression of one day that starts the Glue job
- **D.** An EventBridge Scheduler schedule with a cron expression and a time zone

## Question 10

A curated bucket must survive a Regional outage with a copy elsewhere within 15 minutes of each write. Engineers must also be able to recover from accidental overwrites in the primary bucket. **Choose TWO.**

- **A.** Enable Cross-Region Replication with Replication Time Control to a bucket in another Region
- **B.** Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the primary bucket
- **C.** Add a lifecycle rule that transitions objects to Glacier after one day
- **D.** Enable S3 Versioning on the source and destination buckets
- **E.** Use S3 Batch Operations to copy all objects to another Region weekly

## Question 11

A team of analysts with no coding skills must clean a weekly supplier extract: remove duplicate rows, split a combined name column, and standardize date formats. They want to reuse the same steps every week. What should they use?

- **A.** A Glue Spark job written by the analysts in PySpark from a notebook template
- **B.** AWS Glue DataBrew, saving the steps as a recipe that a scheduled job applies
- **C.** An Athena CTAS query that the analysts copy and edit each week
- **D.** Amazon QuickSight with calculated fields that clean the data during visualization

## Question 12

Glue jobs in private subnets write to S3. The VPC has no internet gateway or NAT gateway. Security also requires that the curated bucket accept requests only from this VPC. **Choose TWO.**

- **A.** Add a NAT gateway and allow its Elastic IP in the bucket policy
- **B.** Create an S3 gateway endpoint and add it to the subnets' route tables
- **C.** Add a bucket policy that denies requests without that aws:SourceVpce
- **D.** Create an interface endpoint for Glue and allow the Glue service principal
- **E.** Turn on Transfer Acceleration and require aws:SecureTransport

## Question 13

Every object uploaded under s3://lab-raw/runs/ must start a validation workflow. The team also wants other teams to subscribe to the same upload events later without changing the bucket configuration. What should the engineer set up?

- **A.** Turn on EventBridge notifications for the bucket and add a rule for the prefix
- **B.** Configure an S3 event notification that invokes the validation Lambda directly
- **C.** Schedule a Lambda function every minute that lists new objects under the prefix
- **D.** Configure CloudTrail data events and have the workflow read the trail files

## Question 14

A lab is moving an on-premises Oracle database with hundreds of stored procedures to Aurora PostgreSQL. It needs an assessment of what converts automatically, the converted schema, and then ongoing row replication until cutover. Which combination should it use?

- **A.** AWS DataSync to copy the Oracle data files and then attach them to Aurora
- **B.** AWS Glue crawlers on the Oracle schema, then Glue ETL jobs for every table
- **C.** AWS DMS full load and CDC alone, letting DMS create the target tables
- **D.** DMS Schema Conversion for assessment and conversion, then DMS full load plus CDC

## Question 15

Managers need an interactive dashboard of daily sequencing output that loads in under two seconds for hundreds of users. The data is refreshed once each morning in Athena. Querying Athena on every page view is slow and adds cost. What should the team do?

- **A.** Point QuickSight at Athena with direct query and enable Athena query result reuse
- **B.** Export the data to CSV each morning and email it to the managers
- **C.** Import the dataset into QuickSight SPICE with a scheduled refresh each morning
- **D.** Build the dashboard in OpenSearch Dashboards over a copy of the Athena tables

## Question 16

A developer starts a Glue job from the console, and it fails reading S3 with AccessDenied. The developer's own role can read the bucket. Which identity's permissions should the engineer fix?

- **A.** The developer's IAM role, because it started the job from the console
- **B.** The job's execution role, which Glue assumes to read and write the data
- **C.** The Glue service-linked role, because it performs all S3 reads for jobs
- **D.** The bucket owner's root user, because only it can grant cross-service access

## Question 17

A Glue job in a private subnet must call a partner's REST API. The partner only accepts connections from IP addresses on its allowlist and asks for one fixed address. What should the engineer set up?

- **A.** An interface VPC endpoint for the partner's API in the job's subnets
- **B.** An Elastic IP address attached directly to the Glue job's network interface
- **C.** An S3 gateway endpoint with a route to the partner's API address range
- **D.** A NAT gateway with an Elastic IP for the private subnet's internet traffic

## Question 18

A crawler runs on s3://lab-raw/runs/ after each daily load. Instead of one partitioned table, it created a separate table for every date folder. The folders contain files with the same schema. What should the engineer configure?

- **A.** Set the crawler's table level so the date folders form one table
- **B.** Change the schema change policy to log changes instead of updating tables
- **C.** Change the recrawl policy so the crawler visits only new folders each day
- **D.** Enable partition projection on each of the date tables the crawler created

## Question 19

A data quality check samples 1% of rows at random from a daily feed of 2 million rows from 40 suppliers. One small supplier sends 0.2% of rows, and its errors keep reaching production unnoticed. What should the team change?

- **A.** Increase the random sample from 1% to 2% of all rows in the daily feed
- **B.** Sample the first 20,000 rows of each file because they arrive first
- **C.** Sample only the largest suppliers because they produce most of the volume
- **D.** Stratify the sample by supplier so every supplier contributes enough rows

## Question 20

A clinical partner requires that donor files be encrypted before they leave its own network, using keys that AWS never sees in plaintext during upload. Files are then stored in S3. What should the partner use?

- **A.** SSE-KMS with a customer managed key that has automatic rotation enabled
- **B.** Client-side encryption, such as the Amazon S3 encryption client, before uploading
- **C.** A bucket policy that denies requests where aws:SecureTransport is false
- **D.** SSE-S3 default encryption combined with S3 Object Lock in compliance mode

## Question 21

A DynamoDB table in on-demand mode throttles writes during a sensor burst, even though total traffic is far below the table limit. Contributor Insights shows one sensor ID receives most writes. Which change addresses the cause?

- **A.** Spread that sensor's writes across several partition keys with a suffix
- **B.** Switch the table to provisioned capacity with much higher write capacity units
- **C.** Add a global secondary index that uses the sensor ID as its partition key
- **D.** Increase the SDK's maximum retry attempts so throttled writes eventually succeed

## Question 22

Two scheduled jobs update the same Redshift summary table every hour. Occasionally one fails with a serializable isolation violation, error 1023. The cluster uses serializable isolation for compliance reasons. What should the engineer do?

- **A.** Run VACUUM and ANALYZE on the summary table before each job starts
- **B.** Change the summary table to DISTSTYLE ALL so each node has its own copy
- **C.** Start each job's transaction with LOCK on the table so the jobs run one at a time
- **D.** Increase the WLM queue's slot count so both jobs get more memory

## Question 23

Messages arrive in an SQS queue. Each message must be filtered to keep only sequencing events, enriched by a Lambda function, and delivered to a Step Functions workflow. The team wants no custom polling code. What should the engineer use?

- **A.** An EventBridge rule on the default bus that matches the queue's messages
- **B.** EventBridge Pipes with the queue as source, a filter, Lambda enrichment, and the workflow target
- **C.** A Lambda function that long-polls the queue and calls StartExecution for each message
- **D.** An SNS topic subscribed to the queue that forwards messages to the workflow

## Question 24

A Lambda function needs a feature flag, an S3 bucket name, and a third-party API token that the vendor rotates by hand twice a year. The team wants the lowest cost and encrypted storage for the token. Where should the values go?

- **A.** All three in Secrets Manager, with a rotation Lambda function for each value
- **B.** All three as plaintext environment variables on the Lambda function
- **C.** The flag and bucket name in Secrets Manager, and the token in environment variables
- **D.** The flag and bucket as Parameter Store parameters, and the token as a SecureString

## Question 25

Twelve instrument types publish events into one Kinesis stream. A fraud-detection consumer and an archival consumer both read it. The fraud-detection consumer lags because the archival consumer's reads use the shared 2 MB/s per shard. What should the engineer do?

- **A.** Create a second stream and have every producer write each event to both streams
- **B.** Increase the stream's retention period so the lagging consumer can catch up later
- **C.** Register the fraud-detection consumer for enhanced fan-out on the stream
- **D.** Replace the stream with an SQS standard queue that both consumers poll

## Question 26

Analysts in Redshift run daily reports that join a 3-billion-row read-count fact table to a 50-row instrument table and a 20-million-row sample table, always joined on sample_id. Which table design reduces data movement during these joins?

- **A.** DISTSTYLE EVEN on all three tables, with a compound sort key on the fact table's date
- **B.** DISTKEY sample_id on the fact and sample tables, with DISTSTYLE ALL or AUTO for instruments
- **C.** DISTSTYLE ALL on the fact table so every node has the full table for the joins
- **D.** DISTKEY instrument_id on the fact table, since every row references an instrument

## Question 27

A pipeline spans Lambda, Glue, and Redshift. When a dashboard shows wrong totals, engineers spend hours matching log lines across services by timestamp. What should the team add to make issues traceable end to end?

- **A.** A batch correlation ID written to every log line, output path, and custom metric
- **B.** Higher log levels, set to DEBUG, in every Lambda function and Glue job
- **C.** CloudTrail data events on every S3 bucket used by the pipeline
- **D.** A separate CloudWatch log group per day for each of the three services

## Question 28

A company sets up SageMaker Unified Studio for its sequencing, clinical, and finance divisions. Each division head must control which of their teams can create projects and which tools those projects get, without involving the central admin. How should it be organized?

- **A.** One AWS account per division, each with its own separate Unified Studio domain
- **B.** One project per division, with every team in the division added as a member
- **C.** One domain, with a domain unit per division whose owner sets project policies
- **D.** One domain, with IAM groups per division attached to the domain's admin role

## Question 29

A genomics team runs thousands of containerized alignment jobs each night. Each job needs 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of memory and runs 20 to 90 minutes. Jobs can be interrupted and retried. The team wants managed queuing with the lowest compute cost. What should it use?

- **A.** AWS Lambda with container images, one invocation for each alignment job
- **B.** An Amazon ECS service with a fixed number of tasks on On-Demand instances
- **C.** Amazon EKS with a self-managed job scheduler on On-Demand nodes
- **D.** AWS Batch job queues on a Spot compute environment with retry strategies

## Question 30

A supplier says next month its feed will rename the column read_cnt to reads and change sample_id from integer to string. Dozens of Athena queries and two Glue jobs read the table. What is the safest rollout?

- **A.** Version the dataset, update readers to handle both formats, validate, then switch
- **B.** Let the nightly crawler update the table schema automatically when the feed changes
- **C.** Ask the supplier to delay forever and reject any file with the new column names
- **D.** Edit the table definition on the day of the change and fix queries as they fail

## Question 31

Someone changed the bucket policy on the curated bucket yesterday and removed a deny statement. Security needs to know which principal made the change and from which IP address. The account has default settings. Where should they look?

## Question 32

A new Glue job only reads s3://lab-raw/runs/ and writes s3://lab-curated/runs/. A developer attached AmazonS3FullAccess to the job role to make it work quickly. Security asks for least privilege. Which policy should replace it?

- **B.** A policy allowing s3:* on both buckets and every object they contain

## Question 33

A Glue job joins instrument records from RDS with run files from S3. In S3, the reads field is sometimes a number and sometimes text. The job fails when writing typed Parquet output. What should the engineer do in the job?
